question: A model that performed well during development has been scored monthly since going live. Its accuracy has declined steadily over eight months, although the code has not changed and no errors have been reported in the data pipeline. What is the most likely explanation?
option_a: The model is gradually forgetting what it learned during its original training process
option_b: The test set used during development must have been unrepresentative of the population
option_c: The conditions the model was trained on have shifted away from current conditions
option_d: Accuracy naturally declines as a model scores a larger cumulative number of records
explanation: A model reflects the conditions it was trained on, and those conditions do not stay fixed.
explanation_a: A deployed model does not change unless it is retrained. Its parameters are fixed, so there is nothing to forget.
explanation_b: An unrepresentative test set would have shown a gap immediately at launch, not a steady decline across eight months.
explanation_c: Customer behaviour, product mixes and processes change over time. A model fixed at training time gradually describes a world that no longer matches the one it is scoring.
explanation_d: Volume alone does not degrade performance. The measure would stay level if conditions held steady.
